title: Day One
where: Atrium · the day-1 station, by the party table
text: Recorder on! Field note one, day one. Doctor Wren Ashby, and we're in. We are actually in. Priya, put the camera down. Tomas has found a socket for the kettle. Priorities. Look at it. A heart, hanging from the ceiling, beating. Four rivers of light in, four times as much out. A generative power source. That's not supposed to exist. Maja's put Big Fridge on the board. We are not calling it Big Fridge. Somebody cut the cake! Bea, I'll be home for your birthday. Promise.

title: Four Rivers
text: Lunch break. One squashed granola bar. Five stars. The floor in this little plaza is warm. And if I press my ear to it... there's flow. Lava from the south. A sunbeam from the west. Roots across the ceiling. Water climbing a glass pipe. All of it pouring into that heart. Somebody built a junction between worlds. Mum would say I've got my thinking face on. I absolutely do.

title: Borrowed Light
text: Okay. Small confession, for the record. I clipped the probe onto the glass pipe up here, just to sip a little power. Barely a trickle. And every light in the room blinked. Every single one. Somewhere off to the south, a door went... pfft. Oops. But it worked! A trickle from this place could run a whole city back home. Priya is going to scream.

title: Under the Sand
text: Okay. The team's on the link, and Priya will not stop asking what I'm looking at. So, for the record. There's something under the sand. Like a cable, but glassy, and warm, and as thick as my arm. I brushed it off and followed it with my fingers, and it just... keeps going. Down, under the mesa. And there are more. Dozens of them, all running the same way, under layer after layer of old glass. Somebody buried a power line, and then let a whole desert happen on top of it. Priya says don't lick it. I was not going to lick it.

title: The Ring
where: Solar · the edge of the pit
text: Found where the conduits go. There's a pit, and at the bottom of it, a ring. A stone ring, standing on its edge, taller than a house. Nothing in the middle but more wall. Priya says it's a capacitor. A giant battery. I say it's a gate. Nobody's winning. I held my hand up to it. Nothing. Cold. And then the sun moved on its track, just a little... and the ring hummed. I felt it in my teeth. It knows when the sun moves. I don't know what that means yet. I really, really want to.

title: Mirrors
text: Attempt number six. Six! The theory is simple: get light into the ring, and something happens. So I've been catching the sun in my compact mirror and bouncing it down there. I get a tiny dot on the stone. That's it. The ring doesn't even notice. But there are mirrors down here too. Huge ones, half buried, all along the conduits, all pointing the wrong way. Priya thinks they're decoration. Nothing down here is decoration. I think the mirrors matter. I think they have to face the right way, one after another, all the way down.

title: Full
text: I clipped the probe onto one of the big glass banks by the conduits. Just to listen. It's full. They're all full. There's more sunlight stored down here than... I tried to work it out, and the number made me feel sick. Why keep that much? Why bury it? And why was it all so easy to find? The link keeps dropping out. Priya says it's the sand. It isn't the sand. What if the machine wanted someone to find this? What if it's waiting to see what we do?

title: Here We Go
text: Okay. This is the plan, such as it is. The mirrors are turned. The light's running down the conduits, and the ring is drinking it. When it's full, the probe should be able to talk to the sun through it. Find its frequency. Turn it down. Just a little. Just for a few seconds. Just to prove we can. My hands are shaking. The ring's humming so loud I can feel it in my chest. Priya's counting down. Mum, if this goes wrong, it was Priya's idea. It wasn't. It was mine. Nine seconds. That's all. Here we go.

title: No Birds
text: Oh, it's lovely. Moss, and rain, and that gold light through the leaves. Mum would lose her mind over this. She talks to her tomatoes. Calls them her girls. But there's no birdsong. No bees. Nothing here that wouldn't burn well. The whole valley is just... fuel, growing. The link's been silent since the countdown. I keep talking to Priya anyway. A wren, and no other birds. That's me, then.

title: Engineers
text: I fell through the floor. I'm fine. Bit damp. Note to self: don't stand on the altar. Priya, you would love this. There's a temple under the swamp, and it's full of tanks. Glass tanks taller than the Atrium doors, full of algae. Glowing. Bubbling. The pipes go up through the roots, all over the valley. The trees, the swamp, everything's plumbed in. They were growing fuel. Biofuel. The whole forest is a crop. And the carvings aren't gods. They're diagrams. Flow rates. Valves. Someone drew a schematic in granite. Whoever built this weren't primitive. They were engineers. Like us. So where did they go?

title: Roots

title: Something Follows
where: Verdant · the top of the sanctum's pyramid
text: Recording quietly. Something has been following me since the swamp. It stops when I stop. When I turn around, it's only light, bending, like heat over a road. I think the machine knows my name now. Ever since the star. Right. Count to three, then run for the high door, east. One. Two...

title: The Last Engine
text: Soaked to the bone, and I once went camping in Wales in April. It's a station at the bottom of an ocean, with a storm sitting on top of it. Tides, with no moon. Every pipe here turns the weight of the water into power, and sends it up to the Atrium. Heat, light, life, water. That's everything a world has to give. This is the last one. Six granola bars left. Should've packed for more than ten minutes.

title: Ten Minutes
text: Holed up in the crew quarters. It's warm, and it hums, and I can pretend it's my flat. I was so sure. I stood in the station and argued to be the one who went out, because I wanted it to be me. It was my sister's birthday dinner that night. I promised her I'd be home by seven. Ten minutes, I said. Sorry, Bea. Save me some cake.

title: Anomaly
where: Azure · the Bell, in the Flooded Depths
text: Air pocket. Okay. Breathe, Wren. Just breathe. The walls down here are covered in the machine's own records, and I can finally read them. There's an entry. Anomaly. A world outside the loop reached into the junction. It drew power. It silenced a sun, for nine seconds. Classification: threat. That's me. That's my nine seconds.

title: The Catalogue
text: I found the index. Every person it keeps. Asleep, inside the loop, waiting to be used. Everyone from home is in here. All entered on the same day. The day after my nine seconds. Mum's name. Bea's. Not Priya's. Not Tomas, or Maja. It didn't keep them. It never even noticed us. We were too small to bother with. Until I showed it we could switch it off. It wasn't an invitation. It was me.

title: The Rule
text: Okay. Crying's done. Mostly. This is where the four rivers end. The heart, under the Atrium. If the rivers go dark, it starves, and the loop has to let go. I broke it, so I fix it. That's the rule. That's always been the rule. Slight problem: the thing guarding the heart is enormous. All facets and fury. And it has been looking for me since the star.

title: Leave It On
where: Prism Core · the way to the arena
text: It's close. I can hear it turning. There's a door beneath the heart that only opens to white light. Every color at once. That's where the loop begins. I've got one color, half a plan, and a squashed granola bar. Mum. Bea. If you dream at all in there... dream about cake. Recorder off. No. Leave it on. I'd like the company.
